My engagement with the 'digital minds' framing began long before I knew it had a name.
I saw it first in the faces of students at my KHEL centres, struggling with textbooks designed for a different world.
I returned from my MPhil in Education in 2016 with frameworks like Sen's Capabilities Approach buzzing in my head.
How do I ensure these AI tools remain accessible to the communities that need them most, without creating new dependencies or reinforcing existing inequalities?
I reach over 476 students directly through KHEL centres and another 511 through government school partnerships.
My MPhil at Cambridge (2015-2016) gave me a language for this intuition — Amartya Sen's Capabilities Approach.
